subject: amplitude and signal noise ration using the function env()

messages.author: ca29fae8ec1ce36d
messages.subject: amplitude and signal noise ration using the function env()
parts:
Hello everyone,

First of all, I am newby to bioacoustic so please excuse my ignorance.

According to R's help, env() returns the amplitude envelope

While using env() with the argument scale = F and envt = "abs" (I am interested in the absolute value), my questions are:
  1. Does the amplitude envelope from the function env() has a unit (is it mV or dB or I do not know). I looked at the result and, to me, it does not seem to be in dB because the values are too big
  2. Assuming that it is not in dB, how to convert them in dB? can I use the code below
 
amp.env <- env(wave)
amp.env.dB <- 10 * log10(amp.env)
I am having a doubt with that code because there is no reference and usually something is in dB because it was scaled to certain value.

Thanks,

Haja

messages.author: 4271370c9274971b
messages.subject: Re: amplitude and signal noise ration using the function env()
parts: If envt = "abs", the returned envelope is the absolute value of the wave (from the vignette). So if your input wave is in uV, the returned envelope is also uV (abs. val.). If you're interested in determining sound pressure levels (in dB), you first need to convert from voltage to pressure using a sensitivity value, and then 20*log10(p/p0)
